title: Segmented KV buckets, preemptive warmup, and scheduler detangle
creator: Asha Patel
description: Replace monolithic LRU-like KV cache with a segmented, TTL-bucketed KV-store and add a lightweight preemptive warmup path. At the same time, remove remaining global scheduler locks by moving to per-core admission buckets and a cooperative handoff path. This reduces tail latencies under bursty traffic and cuts memory fragmentation observed on long-running nodes.
acceptance_criteria: New segmented KV-store is feature-parity for get/put/evict with existing API and passes existing KV behavior tests
End-to-end median and p95 generation latency for synthetic burst tests show >=12% p95 improvement and no >5% regression in median across stable traffic profiles
KV memory fragmentation reduced by measurable amount on long-run heap profiles (heap fragmentation ratio drop >=10%)
Scheduler global lock removed; contention metrics for scheduler_mutex drop to zero in staging
Preemptive warmup successfully primes hot prefixes for 95% of observed hotkeys within 50ms of first appearance in a burst (measured in chaos run)
All changes behind runtime feature flag (segmented_kv_v2) and can be rolled back without cache corruption
implementation_notes: Introduce segmented-kv as an internal store with N independent buckets mapped by high bits of fingerprint to reduce lock contention
Bucket lifecycle: each bucket maintains small LRU for recent keys and a TTL-bucketed freelist for expired entries to avoid sweeping on allocation
Preemptive warmup: sampling agent in ingress path records short-lived hot prefix candidates and issues async warmup tasks that populate KV segments without blocking request path
Scheduler: replace single global admission semaphore with per-core token buckets + cooperative handoff queue; admission logic should consult per-tenant slot budgets
Memory allocator tuning: enable jemalloc arena pinning opt-in and use madvise(DONTNEED) on expired slab pages to reduce RSS growth
Dependency upgrades: bump jemalloc to 5.3.0 and liburing to 2.4 where used by the io adapter; add a compatibility shim in allocator wrapper to fall back if new APIs unavailable
Expose lightweight telemetry hooks: per-bucket hit/miss, warmup success rate, scheduler handoff counts for Console dashboards (sampling only)
Keep legacy kv store code compiled behind feature flag during rollout for quick rollback and A/B comparison
rollout_plan: Merge implementation into feature branch and run full e2e test in staging cluster (runtime:segmented_kv_v2 flag off)
Enable segmented_kv_v2 in canary pool (5% of traffic) with telemetry and compare hit/miss, fragmentation and latency against control for 72 hours
If metrics look healthy, increase to 25% and run chaos tests (node reboots, network flaps) for 48 hours
Full rollout to all regions after success; monitor disk/io and memory metrics closely for 7 days
If any regression >5% p95 or cache corruption suspected, flip feature flag off to rollback immediately
risks: API incompatibility causing subtle cache misreads during rollout—mitigated by strong property tests and feature-flagged compile-time fallback
New allocator tuning may change memory behavior on some instance types—we will gate jemalloc opt-in by instance family for first rollout
Preemptive warmup could overfetch under adversarial traffic patterns and increase token cost—bounded by rate-limiter and sampling thresholds
Scheduler handoff bugs may introduce starvation on very small tenant quotas—covered by integration tests and a conservative default token bucket size
test_plan: Unit tests for segmented-kv get/put/evict semantics and collision stress tests
Property-based tests to verify no key duplication/corruption across bucket boundaries
Microbenchmarks for warmup latency and scheduler admission latency (synthetic bursts + real traffic replay)
Long-running stability run (72h) on staging with memory/fragmentation profiles collected
Chaos engineering scenarios: node restart, OOM injection on a bucket, network partition between shards
Compare Console telemetry in A/B with legacy kv for 7 days before large rollouts
